- Earl Hathaway | | Headquarters | San Francisco, California, United States | | Area served | Worldwide | | Keypeople | Daniel Barber (CEO) | | Products | DataGrail Privacy Management Platform | | Number of employees | 150 (2025)[![Edit this on Wikidata](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/8/8a/OOjs_UI_icon_edit-ltr-progressive.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_edit-ltr-progressive.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q118390931?uselang=en#P1128 "Edit this on Wikidata") | | Website | [www.datagrail.io](https://www.datagrail.io/) | **DataGrail, Inc.** is a data privacy software company headquartered in San Francisco.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-1) The company develops a privacy management platform that helps businesses comply with regulations such as the [GDPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDPR "GDPR"), CCPA, and other global data protection laws.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-3) ## Software \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DataGrail&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Software")\] DataGrail is an [information privacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_privacy "Information privacy") web application developed by DataGrail, Inc.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-4) It is designed to support businesses in adhering to privacy regulations such as the [GDPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Data_Protection_Regulation "General Data Protection Regulation") (General Data Protection Regulation), the [CCPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Consumer_Privacy_Act "California Consumer Privacy Act") (California Consumer Privacy Act), and other global data protection laws.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-8) ## History \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DataGrail&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: History")\] DataGrail, Inc. was founded by Daniel Barber, Ignacio Zendejas, and Earl Hathaway in [Palo Alto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California "Palo Alto, California") in 2018.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-10) DataGrail was available on [Product Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_Hunt "Product Hunt") on May 24, 2018.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-11) The initial product addressed GDPR requirements for [right of access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_of_access_to_personal_data "Right of access to personal data") and [right to be forgotten requests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_be_forgotten "Right to be forgotten").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-12) In September 2018, DataGrail received $4M in investment from Cloud Apps Capital Partners, with participation from [Gunderson Dettmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunderson_Dettmer_Stough_Villeneuve_Franklin_&_Hachigian "Gunderson Dettmer Stough Villeneuve Franklin & Hachigian").[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-13) In October 2019, [Okta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okta,_Inc. "Okta, Inc.") signed a partnership and invested in DataGrail.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-14) The company then released a second product designed in response to [GDPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Data_Protection_Regulation "General Data Protection Regulation") Article 30 requirements. The method for discovering software systems containing [personal data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_data "Personal data") was detailed in a 2020 U.S. patent by Daniel Barber, Ignacio Zendejas, and Earl Hathaway.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-15) In November 2019, [American Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Express "American Express") made a disclosed investment in the company.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-16) In March 2021, DataGrail received $30M in investment from Felicis Ventures and Next47, with participation from [DocuSign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Docusign "Docusign") and [HubSpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HubSpot "HubSpot").[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-17) At the time, the company counted [Databricks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Databricks "Databricks"), [Dexcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dexcom "Dexcom"), and [Twilio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilio "Twilio") among its enterprise customers.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-18) In March 2022, a new funding round led by [Third Point Ventures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Point "Third Point") and [Thomson Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson_Reuters "Thomson Reuters") helped the company raise $45 million. At the same time, DataGrail released a third product designed to conduct [privacy impact assessments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy_impact_assessment "Privacy impact assessment").[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-20) In June 2024, DataGrail released a [consent management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consent_management "Consent management") product to address compliance requirements for global privacy regulations.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-21) In August 2024, the company held the second DataGrail Summit with speakers from Instacart and Anthropic.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-22) In 2025, the company released its annual _Data Privacy Trends Report_, which reported a sharp rise in data deletion requests and increasing compliance costs for businesses handling privacy requests.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-23) ## Awards and recognition \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DataGrail&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Awards and recognition")\] DataGrail has been included in the [Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes") and [Statista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statista "Statista") ranking of America’s Best Startup Employers for three consecutive years, from 2024 to 2026.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-25) In March 2025, [Fast Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Company "Fast Company") included DataGrail in the Most Innovative Companies category for security.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-26)[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-27) The following month, the company won an SC Award in the category Best Compliance Solution for its DataGrail Consent platform.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-28) That same year, DataGrail was included in Built In’s Best Places to Work awards, receiving recognition as both a Top Remote Startup and a Top San Francisco Startup.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-29) In November 2025, DataGrail was recognized as a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Data Privacy Compliance Software vendor assessment.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DataGrail#cite_note-30) ##
